teenKit.tldr: A drug that kills human heart failure patients by forcing their hearts to beat themselves to death actually grants dogs over a year of extra symptom-free life. The secret lies in a tiny, one-ångström atomic shape difference and the unique geometry of different mammalian hearts.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This staggering medical paradox proves that biology isn't one-size-fits-all, forcing scientists to look down at the individual atom to save lives across different species.
keyTakeaways: Milrinone increased human mortality by 28% in the PROMISE trial because over-stimulating human heart enzymes accelerates cardiac burnout.
Pimobendan successfully extended canine Stage B2 survival by 462 days in the EPIC and QUEST trials by sensitizing calcium channels rather than just torching enzymes.
